stories.notes: Story has empty acceptance criteria and describes a complex live preview feature across multiple contexts (GO, UP, MX). Openspec needed first to elaborate AC and define technical scope; speckit then to harden for testability, security (real-time content rendering, multi-tenant isolation), and edge cases.

agentContributions.notes: Novel capability — no live preview mechanism exists in the codebase. useContent is the central attachment point (236 callers). Contentstack live preview SDK integration must plug into its data layer. ACs are empty; VCs derived from description and standard live preview expectations, scoped to our side of the Contentstack API boundary.

Openspec provided empty ACs with a note that this is a novel capability. I built the full list from the story title, file paths, and standard live preview expectations. Key areas covered: (1) Core real-time update behavior (AC-1, AC-2, AC-8), (2) Backward compatibility for 236 useContent callers (AC-3, AC-6), (3) Error handling and fallback (AC-4, AC-5, AC-13), (4) Unsupported content types (AC-7), (5) Accessibility for dynamic updates (AC-9), (6) Performance under rapid updates (AC-10), (7) Production bundle isolation (AC-11), (8) Cleanup/lifecycle (AC-12), (9) ContentstackLink integration (AC-14), (10) Context provider behavior (AC-15). CAVEAT: I do not have access to the file contents — my criteria are inferred from file names and standard Contentstack live preview patterns. If useContent.ts or ContentstackContext.tsx have non-standard APIs, some ACs may need adjustment.

coordinatorReview.reviewNotes: Both agents added meaningful, non-overlapping value: openspec identified the novel capability, the useContent attachment point (236 callers), and scoped VCs to the Contentstack API boundary; speckit then constructed a comprehensive 15-AC set covering real-time behavior, backward compatibility, error handling, accessibility, performance, and lifecycle. However, speckit explicitly states it had no access to file contents and inferred all criteria from file names and standard Contentstack patterns. This is a material risk — if useContent.ts or ContentstackContext.tsx have non-standard APIs, multiple ACs may be incorrect or inapplicable. Additionally, both agents report acceptanceChanged: false despite speckit clearly elaborating acceptance criteria from an empty set, indicating a process/logging gap. Human review needed to validate inferred ACs against actual codebase APIs before implementation.
